subject: Accounting
title: How Tax Brackets Work
description: A 60-second lesson on How Tax Brackets Work.

hook.text: Many people think earning more can push all their income into a higher bracket. That's a myth.

buildup.text: Tax brackets apply rates to portions of income, not the entire amount.

discovery.text: If a bracket taxes 22% above $44,000, only dollars above that threshold pay 22%—not all of them.

twist.text: This means a raise never makes you poorer after tax. Each extra dollar is taxed at its own rate.

climax.text: The marginal system ensures taxation is gradual, not a sudden cliff.

punchline.text: A raise always helps. Tax brackets don't punish earning more.

quiz.question: How do progressive tax brackets work?
options: Higher rates apply only to income above each threshold
All income is taxed at the highest rate
Each bracket has a flat fee

details.summary: Tax brackets divide income into ranges that are each taxed at progressively higher rates, meaning only the income within each bracket is taxed at that bracket's rate — not all of your income at the highest rate you reach.
details.whyItMatters: Misunderstanding tax brackets is one of the most common financial mistakes people make. Knowing how marginal rates work prevents the false belief that earning more can leave you worse off.
takeaways: Tax brackets apply progressively — each dollar is taxed at its own bracket rate, not the top rate
Moving into a higher bracket never makes your total take-home pay decrease
Marginal rate is the rate on your next dollar; effective rate is the average across all your income

faq.question: Does moving into a higher tax bracket mean all my income is taxed at the higher rate?
faq.answer: No. Only the income within the new bracket is taxed at the higher rate. For example, if the 22% bracket starts at $44,725, only dollars earned above that amount are taxed at 22%. Everything below is still taxed at the lower rates. This is called marginal taxation.

faq.question: What is the difference between marginal and effective tax rate?
faq.answer: Your marginal rate is the tax rate on your last (or next) dollar of income — determined by your highest bracket. Your effective rate is the average rate across all your income, which is always lower than your marginal rate because earlier dollars are taxed at lower brackets.
